title: feat(spec)!: a stack's datasources collection refuses a datasource named default, the host-reserved name
body:
Fixes #23634
Clause-②: no

## What

A stack's `datasources` collection now refuses an entry named `default` at authoring: `defineStack`, `os validate` and publish. This is triage's proxy ruling A (issue comment 6189356908).

`default` is the host's primary datasource. The runtime declares and connects it itself (`DefaultDatasourcePlugin`), and `AppPlugin.start()` refuses a stack that declares it in every boot posture. The authoring doors accepted the same stack, so its author met the refusal only after the boot's earlier plugins had started.

- **Where:** a `superRefine` on the stack's `datasources` collection (`STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE` in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`). It is ⛔ not on `DatasourceSchema`, whose documents include the host's own `default` row. The issue is located at `datasources.N.name`, code `custom`. The map form `datasources: { default: { … } }` is refused the same way, because the key normalizes to `name` before the parse.
- **The comparison is the runtime's:** `name === 'default'`, exactly as `app-plugin.ts` compares it. Every other spelling (`Default`, `' default'`, …) is already refused by `DatasourceSchema.name`'s snake_case pattern, never by this rule.
- **The text:** it carries the runtime's sentence ("declares a datasource named 'default' — that name is reserved for the host's primary datasource") and the ruling's remedy: set `OS_DATABASE_URL` and omit the entry, or declare the datasource under another name and route objects to it (an object's `datasource`, or a `datasourceMapping` rule).
- **ADR-0087:** D3 semantic entry `stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused`. The changeset `.changeset/23634-stack-datasource-default-refused.md` is a BREAKING `minor` (pre mode) with the `registered` disposition, the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix.
- **Dropped-refinements ledger:** `z.toJSONSchema()` has no arm for a refinement, so the published JSON Schema stays wider than the parse at the four installed-package `manifest.datasources` sites. These are recorded in `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json` (+4 sites, total 759 → 763), as the build requires. No arm of the closed `refinement-projection.ts` list fits ("an element's `name` is not X"). Adding one is a public-contract decision, so it is not made here.

Untouched, as the ruling and the claim require: `DatasourceSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts`), `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (PR #23631's remedy line stays as written), `skills/**`, and `content/docs/releases/`.

## Fallback clause: no config that boots today is newly refused

I re-measured this on this branch, using the source CLI (`bin/run-dev.js serve`) on a host config that declares `datasources: [{ name: 'default', driver: 'sqlite', … }]`. The fixture uses `defineStack(…, { strict: false })` so that the boot is what judges it.

- With `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:…`: exit 1, `[AppPlugin] app 'com.example.fx' declares a datasource named 'default' — that name is reserved for the host's primary datasource. …`
- With `--dev`: exit 1, the same refusal.

These agree with the readings dev's M2, M3 and M4 and with production M1 (PR #23631's no-storage refusal), all in the report on #23634. In-repo producers of the shape: none. The candidates `git grep` found are a runtime pin that feeds a raw bundle to `AppPlugin` (still green, 12/12), REST/metadata-door tests of the host's own row, and engine driver maps. None of them goes through the stack collection.

## Pins

- `packages/spec/src/stack-datasource-host-reserved-name.test.ts` (7 tests):
  - `defineStack` refuses the array form and the map form with `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422, one issue at `datasources.N.name`;
  - the bare `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` parse refuses it;
  - the reserved set is the runtime's;
  - CONTROL: `fx_primary` passes;
  - CONTROL: the host's own `default` row parses through `DatasourceSchema`.
- `packages/cli/test/stack-datasource-default-validate-door.test.ts` (integration tier, 2 spawns): `os validate --json` exits 1 with exactly one error, `custom` at `datasources.0.name`, carrying the sentence and `OS_DATABASE_URL`. CONTROL: the same stack with `fx_primary` exits 0 with `valid: true`.

## Verification

Measured on head `a6f3e6e8`, which is this branch merged with `origin/main` `a869ea63` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`. Pre-merge readings are on `a085cc9b`.

- **spec:**
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`: exit 0.
  - `check:generated`: all 14 artifacts up to date.
  - The pin file, `scripts/dropped-refinements.test.ts` and `src/migrations/migrations.test.ts`: 212/212.
  - Full `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` on the pre-merge tree: 679 files passed. The one red was the ledger's header total, fixed in `109c9e90` and then 27/27.
  - `typecheck`: exit 0.
- **cli:**
  - The door pin: 2/2 on the merge head.
  - `vitest run --project unit`: 295 files. 293 passed in the first run; the other 2 read `packages/cli/dist`, which was not built yet, and passed (29/29) after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`.
  - `typecheck`: exit 0.
- **runtime:** `src/default-datasource-plugin.test.ts` 12/12. The `AppPlugin` refusal is unchanged.
- **Ablation** (the refusal body made a no-op, `if ((globalThis as any).__ablation23634 === undefined) return;`, via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`):
  - **Mutated:** the spec build exited 0, and `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 12 dist files. The spec pins went 4 failed / 3 passed: the four refusals red, the three controls green. The CLI door went 1 failed / 1 passed: the refusal red, the control green.
  - **Restored:** `git diff HEAD` was empty and the hash matched HEAD. The rebuild exited 0, and the preflight `--absent` was clean in all 232 files. Spec pins 7/7, CLI door 2/2.
  - **Two earlier legs were no-ops and are not counted:**
    - Deleting the `.superRefine` failed the mutated build on the dropped-refinements ledger, so `dist/` stayed unmutated (the preflight caught it).
    - A string-literal guard was constant-folded out of `dist/` (the preflight `planted` check read absent).
- **Derived gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 90 families for the 6 changed paths. On `a085cc9b` all 90 exit 0, and `--ran` reconciled 90 derived / 90 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED, a derived zero with every exit code recorded.
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` first exited 3 on the shallow clone and passed after fetching its pinned fixture commit.
  - `check:stack-collection-maps` was red on a multi-line `z\n.array(` that hid `datasources` from its census. It was fixed in `a085cc9b` by keeping `z.array(DatasourceSchema)` on one line.
  - **Rerun on the merge head `a6f3e6e8`:** the same 90 families, all exit 0. `--ran` reconciled 90 / 90 / 0 NOT-MEASURED, a derived zero.
- `check:adr-0087-registration`: ✓, `registered stack-datasource-host-reserved-name-refused (new here)`. `check:dev-prereqs`: exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- **Skills line, for the skills lane (⛔ not edited here).** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md:4-6` reads: "Objects route to one via their `datasource` field (default: `'default'`). Most apps need only the `default` datasource; declare more to read/write a **separate** or **external** database." "Declare more" implies that `default` is declared too, so it reads as an invitation. Suggested rewording: "Most apps need only the host's `default` datasource, which the host connects from `OS_DATABASE_URL`; never declare a datasource named `default` (the name is host-reserved and refused). Declare a datasource under its own name only to read/write a **separate** or **external** database."
- **One sentence, three sites.** The runtime's refusal (`app-plugin.ts`), the admin door (`datasource-admin-service.ts`) and this one are synonymous, not shared. The shared text could be exported from spec and reused by the runtime, but that needs a `packages/runtime` edit, which is outside this claim. It is reported, not done.
